summary: The XRD analysis in this paper compares CsPbBr3 perovskite quantum dots (PQDs) before and after ligand exchange with different thiol ligands. All samples exhibit identical peak positions, indicating preservation of the perovskite crystal structure. Ligand exchange leads to increased XRD peak intensities, suggesting improved crystallinity or preferred orientation, but no new phases or significant structural changes are detected. The absence of FWHM and quantitative phase analysis limits the ability to assess crystallite size or microstrain effects.

key_findings.finding: XRD peak positions remain unchanged after ligand exchange, indicating the crystal structure of CsPbBr3 PQDs is preserved.
XRD peak intensities increase after ligand exchange, suggesting enhanced crystallinity or preferred orientation.

scientific_interpretation.claim: Ligand exchange with either ExMP or ExOT does not alter the crystal phase of CsPbBr3 PQDs, as evidenced by identical XRD peak positions across all samples.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: All samples (before and after ligand exchange) show the same set of XRD peak positions, indicating no phase change.

scientific_interpretation.claim: The increase in XRD peak intensities after ligand exchange suggests improved crystallinity or a change in preferred orientation of the CsPbBr3 PQDs.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: The analysis notes that peak intensities increase after ligand exchange, which is commonly associated with improved crystallinity or orientation effects.

citations.evidence: Peak intensities increase after ligand exchange

scientific_interpretation.claim: No evidence of new phases or significant structural transformation is observed after ligand exchange.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: No new peaks appear and all peak positions are unchanged, indicating the absence of new crystalline phases.

limitations.claim: FWHM values are not reported, preventing quantitative assessment of crystallite size or microstrain.
No quantitative phase analysis or lattice parameter refinement is provided, limiting the ability to detect subtle structural changes.
Interpretation of increased peak intensity as improved crystallinity or orientation is not directly confirmed without supporting data such as texture analysis or TEM.
